title: Introduce soft capacity fence and ephemeral priority allocator to reduce autoscaler thrash and improve microburst fairness
author: Aisha Khan
release_notes: Adds a configurable soft capacity fence to reduce scale-up/scale-down oscillation and a short-lived ephemeral priority allocator to fairly distribute microburst credits across tenants. Includes telemetry and feature flag gating.
description: Context: We continue to see autoscaler thrash in medium-load bursts where short-lived demand spikes cause the fleet to scale up then immediately scale down, destabilizing warm pools and increasing cost. Small tenants with occasional microbursts are starved by aggressive proportional allocators and end up timing out while larger steady tenants consume most freshly provisioned slots. Motivation: Reduce churn from transient headroom changes, provide a bounded short-term priority channel for microbursts, and surface observability for fence violations and ephemeral allocations. This PR introduces two cooperating mechanisms: 1) A soft capacity fence that prevents immediate reclamation of recently provisioned capacity for a configurable grace window and a decay curve rather than an instantaneous release. The fence is applied per-fleet and per-tenant reservation waterfall; it is soft because it permits reclamation for higher-severity events (e.g., critical safety drains) but biases the autoscaler to prefer gentle ramp-down. 2) An ephemeral priority allocator: a transient, time-bounded pool of priority credits that can be loaned to tenants when they emit validated microburst requests. Credits are repaid via a short throttling phase or via scheduled background demotion; the allocator enforces strict fairness windows to prevent long-term priority accumulation. Design notes: - The soft fence is implemented as a headroom token ledger with timestamps and a decaying headroom score (RFC-style parameters: fence_window_seconds, decay_half_life_seconds, reclaim_threshold_percent). - Ephemeral allocator is a scoped priority pool (config: pool_size_slots, max_credit_duration_seconds, per_tenant_credit_cap) and integrates with the request admission path so that ephemeral allocations are only granted when latency SLO for the router is preserved. - Both features are behind an operator-controllable feature flag (feature.gate.soft_capacity_fence / feature.gate.ephemeral_allocator) and default to off for existing Dedicated fleets. - Telemetry adds metrics: redwood_fence_allocated_seconds, redwood_fence_reclaims_total, redwood_ephemeral_credit_grants_total, redwood_ephemeral_credit_rejections_total, redwood_ephemeral_grant_latency_ms. Also added tracing spans for fence-eval and ephemeral-grant with contextual tags (tenant_id, fleet_id, reason). Migration & rollout: - Default to gated rollout for 72 hours in staging fleets, then gradual rollout across small fleets (<= 50 GPUs) with canary monitoring. - If fence_violation_rate > 1% or ephemeral_grant_rejection_rate > 10% in canaries, the feature gate will be rolled back automatically by the ops runbook. Testing: - Unit tests for ledger decay math, allocator fairness window, and gating logic. - Integration harness: synthetic microburst scenarios showed 48% reduction in scale-up events vs master and 22% lower cold-start tail latency for microburst tenants. - Load test: 6-hour rerun on perf-canary cluster with mixed tenant profiles (50% steady, 50% bursty) preserved 99th-percentile generation latency within SLO and reduced total scale events by 34%. Backwards compatibility: - Existing reservation semantics are preserved when the feature flags are off. - Rollback is safe because reclamation remains policy-governed; no immediate resource leaks. Configuration: - New API surface in fleet config: soft_capacity_fence: {enabled, fence_window_seconds, decay_half_life_seconds, reclaim_threshold_percent} and ephemeral_priority: {enabled, pool_size_slots, max_credit_duration_seconds, per_tenant_credit_cap}. Observability: - Console dashboard tile added for fence state per-fleet and ephemeral pool utilization. - Alerts: fence_violation_rate (warning) and ephemeral_pool_exhaustion (critical). Security/permissions: - Only operators with fleet-admin role can toggle the feature gates. Related work: ENG-1482 (autoscaler stability spike investigation), ENG-1709 (microburst fairness doc).

review_conversation: Jonah Pierce: High-level LGTM. Two requests: (1) can we make the default decay_half_life conservative so small canaries are safe? (2) Add a metric to count per-tenant grant latency buckets
Aisha Khan: Answered — default decay_half_life_seconds is 600s in config; increased canary to 1200s for initial rollout. Added per-tenant grant latency histogram in telemetry commit.
Lin Wei: Thread-safety nit in headroom_ledger.go: prefer atomic.RWMutex vs atomic counters for map ops. Also question about reclaim priority vs safety drains.
Aisha Khan: Addressed with a map-level RWMutex and microbenched; added early-return path to allow immediate reclaim on operator/drain events.
Caroline Voss: Tests look good; please add an e2e assertion that ephemeral grants do not exceed per_tenant_credit_cap under high contention
Aisha Khan: Added e2e assertion and extended perf-run to 6 hours. Reran CI and green.
merge_outcome_summary: Merged into main after addressing concurrency nit and adding e2e cap assertion. CI passed on final run (all checks green). Rollout gated; ops instructed to follow canary runbook. Observed 34% fewer scale events in perf canary with preserved latency SLOs.
